Keratoconus Treatment: Everything You Need to Know

Keratoconus is a progressive eye condition that affects the shape of the cornea—the clear, dome-shaped surface at the front of the eye. Instead of maintaining a smooth, round curvature, the cornea gradually becomes thinner and bulges outward into a cone shape, leading to distorted vision.

Understanding this condition and seeking timely treatment can help preserve your eyesight and prevent complications.

What Causes Keratoconus?

The exact cause is not always known, but several factors may contribute:

Genetic predisposition
Excessive eye rubbing
Chronic allergies
Connective tissue disorders
Long-term UV exposure

Treatment Options for Keratoconus
Treatment depends on the severity and progression of the condition.
1. Eyeglasses or Soft Contact Lenses
2. Rigid Gas Permeable (RGP) Lenses
3. Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking (CXL)
4. Intacs (Corneal Implants)
5. Corneal Transplant
